bull_bear.body: Prioritizing high-return niche projects; reducing capex intensity post-FY26; using cash flow to reduce net debt; funding backward integration and JV via debt/equity mix; no dividend policy mentioned.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical disruption in Middle East (feedstock access); prolonged raw material volatility; labor shortages delaying Zone IV commissioning; working capital pressure from export receivables; China policy uncertainty in agrochem; FX exposure on unhedged $87M loan.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic; transparent on delays (labor, LPG, elections); confident in long-term contracts and operational leverage; focused on margin recovery via China supply contraction and integration; acknowledges near-term headwinds but emphasizes resilience and strategic positioning.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: INR39cr FX loss is accounting artifact (unhedged loan) with natural hedge via exports; inventory surge of INR409cr is transit goods (not recognized as revenue); labor shortage is region-specific (LPG + election migration), not systemic; Zone IV EBITDA potential unchanged despite delays; net debt normalization already underway (cash used to repay debt in April).
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Stated financial targets: 'Target EBITDA range of Rs. 1,800-2,200 Cr; Debt/EBITDA of <2.5x and ROCE of >15%'.
- Growth outlook is volume-led: 'Consistent volume growth over 3 yrs driven by increased capacities, despite margin pressures'.
- Balance sheet pressure flagged: 'Working capital increased due to increase in exports. Resulting in increase in debt and finance costs.'
- Currency exposure is unhedged on part of the borrowings — finance costs include a revaluation impact of about Rs. 39 crs on unhedged foreign currency long term loans caused by steep depreciation of the rupee versus the dollar.
- Spending is being directed to capex (about Rs. 1125 Cr in FY26) and JVs; the deck makes no mention of dividend, buyback or debt-reduction plans.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Integrated operations across the benzene and toluene value chains — efficient production, cost optimisation and steady internal supply of raw materials for downstream products.
- Global scale position: ranks 4th globally for approximately 75% of its product portfolio and is a recognised leader in chlorination, nitration and hydrogenation chemistries.
- Effective management of co-products and isomers — by-product processing improves cost efficiency, creates additional revenue streams and supports sustainability (the calcium chloride plant exists to gainfully utilise by-products).
- Process chemistry scale-up expertise and a strategically distributed network of R&D and pilot plants, with two advanced R&D centres, 250+ scientists including 20+ PhDs, a 12,000 sq. ft. analytical laboratory and an 8,000 sq. ft. process safety laboratory.
- Expertise in complex chemistries — photochemistry, vapour phase chemistry and Grignard chemistry — enabling robust, cost-effective processes for rapid scale-up.
- Customer switching costs and stickiness through CRDMO / custom synthesis engagement from concept development to commercial manufacturing, plus long-term contracts with global partners (including a residual 15-year contract and a supply agreement running to March 2030).
- Multipurpose manufacturing assets that reduce time-to-market and allow rapid response to emerging customer requirements across multiple chemistry platforms.
- Ability to meet strict quality standards for regulated sectors — pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals and personal care — supported by SPC, Annual Product Quality Reviews and a central repository of 1,600+ product specifications, 320+ standard test procedures and 70+ general test procedures.
- Wide range of end-use applications across pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, polymers, dyes and personal care, reducing dependence on any single sector.
- Customised delivery solutions including near-to-plant stock points, and a logistics control centre monitoring 1,000+ vehicles carrying approximately 350 chemical variants with GPS tracking and 24x7 emergency response across a stated 3,500-km network.
- Long-standing customer relationships — over 85% of revenue is generated from customers with relationships spanning more than 10 years (per the value-creation capitals disclosure).
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Trade and tariffs — US tariffs on Indian chemical exports — Management flags that US tariffs are creating pricing pressure and eroding competitiveness against European and Chinese suppliers. Structural because exports are 57% of turnover and the company serves more than 400 international customers across 60 countries. Mitigation is proactive diversification of the export mix towards Europe, the Middle East and Africa, strategic recalibration of the US approach, and proactive customer renegotiations; MD&A notes US volumes resumed as India-US trade dynamics improved.
- Competitive intensity from China, particularly in agrochemicals, pharmaceuticals and fluoro products — Intense pricing pressure and hyper-competition from Chinese suppliers keeps margins under pressure even where volumes are stable — MD&A states agrochemicals and pharma remained stable in volume but continued to face margin pressure from global oversupply and Chinese competition. Mitigation is indigenous technology to be a lowest-cost producer, a shift from bulk products to high-value application-led advanced materials, and monitoring of China's anti-involution policy and the removal of VAT export rebates.
- Raw material price volatility and inventory valuation losses — Steep corrections in input prices (benzene and aniline) lead to inventory valuation losses and pricing volatility across the value chain; the first quarter of FY 2025-26 was explicitly impacted by raw material price corrections and inventory losses. Mitigation is new pricing formulas in long-term raw material contracts, long-term methanol and toluene feedstock contracts across the GCC and Southeast Asia, and AI/digital tools for real-time process control.
- Financial and working capital risk — leverage tied to the export-led model and the capex cycle — Increased reliance on exports lengthens credit profiles and raises working capital requirements, debt and interest costs; working capital rose on higher exports, elevated raw material prices and inventory tied up in export shipments awaiting delivery and revenue recognition. Management describes net debt closing marginally above the level implied by a Net Debt-to-EBITDA of 3.7x, and mitigates through capital discipline, a tapering capex approach and a focus on medium-ticket projects with attractive payback and high ROCE.
- Project execution and commissioning delays at the Zone IV growth platform — Execution timelines slipped 3-4 months due to labour constraints, commercial LPG availability issues and election-related workforce migration; the MPP and PEDA facilities remain in commissioning trials, and toluene-chain Zone IV blocks shifted by three to four months on labour availability and geopolitical factors. Structural because Zone IV is the flagship growth platform whose revenue contribution underpins the expected deleveraging and margin expansion.
- Operational and supply-chain dependence on critical raw materials, notably chlorine for new downstream facilities — Potential disruptions in the supply of critical raw materials such as chlorine for new downstream facilities are explicitly flagged; mitigated by entering long-term strategic partnerships with domestic suppliers, including the exclusive chlorine supply arrangement with DCM Shriram Limited serving the Zone IV Jhagadia facility through dedicated pipeline infrastructure.
- Geopolitical and logistical disruption — Regional conflicts caused shipping delays, vessel rerouting, port congestion at Kandla and intermittent production at the Kutch facility, alongside elevated freight costs and logistics bottlenecks. Mitigated by commercial agility in redirecting trade flows and by holding higher inventory (1.5 to 2 months) of key raw materials such as aniline for production security.
- Single-segment and geographic concentration — Structural concentration risk not labelled as such: the Group reports only one reporting segment under Ind AS 108, 100% of turnover comes from chemical manufacture (NIC 201/202), and the manufacturing footprint is concentrated in a few Gujarat/Maharashtra sites (Vapi, Tarapur, Jhagadia, Dahej, Kutch), so a site- or sector-level shock is not diversified away.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Energy (40% rev): volumes down 4% QoQ due to Middle East disruptions; MMA shipments diverted to US/Europe; capacity expansion to 360 KTPA on track. Agrochemical: steady volume growth; margin pressure persists but China supply disruptions may improve spreads. Dyes/pigments: stable; demand destruction in low-margin segments possible. Polymers: strong growth driven by EV demand; MPDA underperforming due to Chinese competition. Pharma: stable; China anti-involution to benefit PNCB/NCB chain from Q1FY27.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Established by first generation technocrats in 1984; the deck's stated moat is 'Integrated operations and high-cost optimization', strong R&D capabilities with IPRs for customized products, and a strategic location in western India with proximity to ports.
- Key value chains named as Nitro Chloro Benzenes, Di-Chlorobenzenes, Phenylenediamines, Nitro Toluene value chain and Sulphuric Acid & downstream, grouped under benzene-based downstream, toluene-based downstream, sulphuric acid products and other speciality chemicals.
- Scale markers at a glance: 100+ products, 1,100+ domestic and global customers, 60 exporting countries, 16 manufacturing plants, 2 state-of-the-art R&D centres and 6000+ employees.
- Customer relationships are framed as structural partnerships covering feedstock assurance and supply, technology sharing, joint product development and manufacturing outsourcing; the vision is 'To emerge as a Global Partner of Choice for leading consumers of speciality chemicals and intermediates'.
- Long-term ambition includes promoting 'India as manufacturing destination of choice', partnering customers for new India-based investments, and leveraging R&D strength to provide CDMO services to key clients.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Contract] Entered into a 4-year supply contract for an existing product with a target revenue of about $150 mn; 'The customer is an existing customer. AIL has adequate capacities to meet the contract volumes.' Separately, 2 additional long term contracts were signed in Q4 and existing long term contracts are 'progressing well and remain stable'.
- [Trade & tariffs] US tariffs and Chinese competition are pressuring PDA; US volumes are 'resuming post the India US trade deal'; and the US Deal, EU FTA and China's anti-involution stance are expected to improve the mid-term outlook for agrochemicals.
- [China anti-involution] Cited as supporting margin upticks and volumes in PNCB and the NCB chain towards the end of Q4FY26, even as 'Margin pressure especially in fluoro products from China persists'.
- [Geopolitical / feedstock risk] Volumes in UAE / Oman were impacted by the West Asia crisis, which is also expected to 'impact the availability of critical feed stocks', with AIL 'taking necessary steps to mitigate the situation'; energy volatility linked to refining margins adds near-term risk to Gasoline-Naphtha cracks.
- [Zone IV timing conflict] The application slide says customer engagement was 'Initiated ... for Zone IV products expected to come on stream gradually from Q4FY26', while the outlook slide in the same (May 2026, post-Q4FY26) deck says Zone IV projects are delayed by 3-4 months — both readings are recorded rather than reconciled.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Established in 1984 by first-generation technocrats and headquartered in Mumbai, AIL manufactures speciality chemicals built on chlorination, nitration and hydrogenation chemistries, with core value chains in Nitro Chloro Benzenes (NCB), Dichlorobenzenes (DCB), Phenylenediamines (PDA) and Nitro Toluene (NT), alongside a sulphuric acid and calcium chloride chain. These intermediates feed downstream applications across agrochemicals, pharmaceuticals, polymers, fuel additives, dyes and pigments, and the Company is also a leading manufacturer and exporter of performance-enhancing octane boosters for the energy sector. AIL is shifting from bulk product manufacturing to a knowledge-driven, application-led and platform-led model — combining integrated chemistry platforms, multipurpose assets, CRDMO/custom synthesis and customer co-creation — serving over 1,100 customers across more than 60 countries, with the Board's Report describing it as no longer just a manufacturer but an Integrated Chemistry Solution Provider.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Benzene value chain:** Nitro Chloro Benzenes (NCB), Di-Chlorobenzenes (DCB), Phenylenediamines (PDA), PNCB, MDCB, PDCB, Chloroanilines
- **Toluene value chain:** Nitro Toluene (NT), Chlorotoluene and downstream process blocks, Downstream ethylation chain products, PEDA (advanced intermediate)
- **Sulphuric acid chain:** Sulphuric acid, Calcium chloride
- **Energy:** Mono Methyl Aniline (MMA), Octane boosters / fuel-blending additives
- **Agrochemicals and Fertilisers:** Nitro Toluene and downstream ethylation products, Critical intermediate for crop protection formulations, PEDA
- **Pharmaceuticals:** PNCB, MDCB, Fluorinated compounds
- **Dyes, Pigments and Printing Inks:** NCBs, 3,3-DCBH
- **Polymers and Additives:** PDCB (EV-linked PPS applications), DCB chain derivatives, PCBTF
- **Emerging platforms:** Advanced materials, Electronic chemicals, Advanced / high-performance engineering polymers, Semiconductor value chain materials, Circular economy solutions, Clean energy value chain products

business.title: Group structure (profile)

business.body:
- Integrated operations across the benzene and toluene value chains — efficient production, cost optimisation and steady internal supply of raw materials for downstream products.
- Global scale position: ranks 4th globally for approximately 75% of its product portfolio and is a recognised leader in chlorination, nitration and hydrogenation chemistries.
- Effective management of co-products and isomers — by-product processing improves cost efficiency, creates additional revenue streams and supports sustainability (the calcium chloride plant exists to gainfully utilise by-products).
- Process chemistry scale-up expertise and a strategically distributed network of R&D and pilot plants, with two advanced R&D centres, 250+ scientists including 20+ PhDs, a 12,000 sq. ft. analytical laboratory and an 8,000 sq. ft. process safety laboratory.
- Expertise in complex chemistries — photochemistry, vapour phase chemistry and Grignard chemistry — enabling robust, cost-effective processes for rapid scale-up.
- Customer switching costs and stickiness through CRDMO / custom synthesis engagement from concept development to commercial manufacturing, plus long-term contracts with global partners (including a residual 15-year contract and a supply agreement running to March 2030).
- Multipurpose manufacturing assets that reduce time-to-market and allow rapid response to emerging customer requirements across multiple chemistry platforms.
- Ability to meet strict quality standards for regulated sectors — pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals and personal care — supported by SPC, Annual Product Quality Reviews and a central repository of 1,600+ product specifications, 320+ standard test procedures and 70+ general test procedures.
- Wide range of end-use applications across pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, polymers, dyes and personal care, reducing dependence on any single sector.
- Customised delivery solutions including near-to-plant stock points, and a logistics control centre monitoring 1,000+ vehicles carrying approximately 350 chemical variants with GPS tracking and 24x7 emergency response across a stated 3,500-km network.
- Long-standing customer relationships — over 85% of revenue is generated from customers with relationships spanning more than 10 years (per the value-creation capitals disclosure).

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- 'Chemistries of Collaboration' — a deliberate, execution-focused operating paradigm combining flexible manufacturing assets, disciplined capital allocation and long-term alignments with global customers, positioning AIL as the Global Partner of Choice in speciality chemicals.
- Shift focus from a multi-year capex cycle to maximising asset utilisation and improving capital efficiency now that the cycle is concluding.
- Drive a higher contribution from advanced materials and specialty products, reducing dependence on commoditised bulk chemicals.
- Disciplined capital allocation with a minimum pre-tax ROCE threshold of 20% for new investments, and improving current ROCE (~8%) through higher utilisation, better product mix and operational efficiencies.
- Strengthen the balance sheet — reduce net debt-to-EBITDA from 3.7x to below 2.5x through strong free cash flow generation.
- Partnership-led growth: JVs and supply alliances (Superform Chemistries JV, RESL recycling platform, Actylis distribution, DCM Shriram raw-material supply, and a customer-linked backward-integration project) to enhance integration, reduce supply risk and strengthen long-term earnings visibility.
- Forward integration and commercialisation of the capital already invested — Zone IV at Jhagadia transitioning from a construction site to a commercial powerhouse and serving as the launchpad into high-margin, specialised downstream chemistries.
- Structural cost optimisation across the value chain — lean operational baseline, optimised procurement and dynamic pricing models to limit profitability deterioration in volatile quarters.
- Digital and AI-led operations — AI, digital twins and predictive maintenance across critical process blocks, shifting from reactive to proactive plant management.
- Green transition — scaling a hybrid renewable energy portfolio to structurally lower baseline operating costs while meeting carbon footprint reduction targets.
- Geographic rebalancing of the export book — actively scaling presence and market share in Europe, the Middle East and Africa to offset localised softness, while working with North American partners to absorb part of the new U.S. tariffs rather than exiting key markets.
- Leadership and governance transition — Suyog Kotecha leads as CEO & Executive Director while Rajendra Gogri, Rashesh Gogri and Renil Gogri transition to Non-Executive Board leadership roles providing strategic guidance and stewardship.
- Safety and zero-harm as a stated highest priority, with behavioural safety and operational discipline embedded across every manufacturing facility.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: FY 2025-26 was described as the peak phase of Aarti's investment cycle, with capex of about ₹ 1,125 Crs directed primarily at the Zone IV platform at Jhagadia plus fast-track capacity additions in MMA, DCB and PEDA-related initiatives. Zone IV is the flagship growth platform and forms part of a total build-out of ₹ 1,600-1,800 Crs. During the year the calcium chloride plant (Phase I, in Zone IV) completed commercial runs and is ramping up, while the multipurpose plant (MPP), the 4,000 TPA PEDA facility and related downstream units advanced through commissioning stages; execution timelines slipped by 3-4 months because of labour constraints, commercial LPG availability issues and election-related workforce migration, so the MPP and PEDA facilities remain in commissioning trials. Under the strategy chapter, FY27 commissioning includes the multi-purpose plant and the 4,000 TPA PEDA facility, followed by photochlorination, hydrolysis and nitration blocks; management also plans to increase capacity from 290 KTPA to 360 KTPA and to expand DCB capacity from 120 KTPA serving fuel additives to 140 KTPA aimed at EV-linked PPS demand, and to advance the Superform Chemistries Limited JV. A recycling/circular-chemistry platform linked to Re Sustainability (the Re Aarti initiative) and the Augene (Superform) JV are both targeted for commissioning in FY27. Backward integration continues through a ₹ 200-250 Crs capex initiative with a global customer tied to the residual 15-year long-term contract, alongside a USD 150 million supply agreement with a global agrochemical innovator running to March 2030 that adds revenue visibility with no incremental capex. Input security was strengthened by long-term methanol and toluene feedstock contracts across the GCC and Southeast Asia and by an exclusive chlorine supply partnership with DCM Shriram Limited feeding Zone IV Jhagadia through dedicated pipeline infrastructure. From FY 2026-27 capex is expected to moderate to ₹ 750-800 Crs, and elsewhere is described as declining significantly to well below ₹ 1,000 Crs given the absence of major greenfield projects, with spending mainly on Zone IV completion, contract-linked projects and routine maintenance; Zone IV is entering its revenue-generation phase with initial commercial revenue expected from the second half of FY 2026-27 and rising gradually as utilisation improves. The disclosed footprint stands at 16 manufacturing facilities, 5 co-generation power plants, over 100 products, 4 R&D centres including 2 pilot plants, and 16 national plant locations with 2 national and 3 international offices; 8 plants are Zero Liquid Discharge and 3 more ZLD-ready. Note: this bundle contains no dated installed-capacity disclosure table, so installed_capacity is left empty — the KTPA figures above are stated as expansion plans, not as a dated capacity schedule.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Speciality and knowledge-led chemicals are estimated to grow at nearly 1.5 times GDP growth, driven by structural demand from the energy transition, electric vehicles, semiconductor localisation, sustainable agriculture, electronics, high-performance polymers and advanced manufacturing.
- A 'two-speed' chemicals market: commodity and bulk chemicals face overcapacity, intense competition and margin compression from China's capacity additions, while speciality/knowledge-led segments show stronger resilience through higher value addition and customer integration.
- China's anti-involution drive and supply-side rationalisation (tougher environmental benchmarks, state-led consolidation phasing out inefficient capacity over the 15th Five-Year Plan) are expected to restore pricing discipline; management expects gradual normalisation and a 'competitiveness window' for Indian exporters.
- The global shift from 'Just-in-Time' efficiency to 'Just-in-Case' preparedness — supplier diversification, inventory flexibility, regional sourcing and long-term supply assurance — creating substantial opportunity to secure long-term CDMO contracts and joint ventures.
- Structural shifts in global trade favouring India as a manufacturing hub: the concluded India-EU FTA and improving U.S.-India trade dynamics are lowering tariff barriers for high-end specialty chemicals and opening new corridors for the Advanced Materials portfolio, with a strong pipeline of product qualifications and commercial discussions underway.
- India's push to reduce dependence on China for key intermediates creates an import-substitution opportunity, encouraging deeper capabilities across critical chemistries and better backward integration.
- EV-linked PPS demand is driving increasing customer traction for Dichlorobenzene, with a visible growth pipeline.
- Improved capacity utilisation — collaboration and long-term customer alignment lifted utilisation to about 80% across all key products, enhancing customer stickiness and margin resilience.
- EBITDA margins stabilised at approximately 13% to 14% and improved sequentially in the second half of the year as cost optimisation took effect.
- Exports account for approximately 57% of total revenues, with the U.S. market seeing a gradual recovery in volumes during the year.
- Management expects FY27 to deliver improved utilisation, margin expansion and a meaningful inflexion in free cash flows.
- Zone IV expansion is expected to contribute meaningfully to revenue and margins from FY28 onwards.
- Digitalisation gains are already measurable — over ₹100 Cr of variable and fixed cost improvement and 30%+ Y-o-Y volume growth attributed to AI, digital twins and predictive maintenance deployment.
- The Indian chemical industry is estimated at USD 155-165 billion and projected to reach USD 230-255 billion by 2030 (around 8-9% CAGR); the global chemical industry is expected to grow 3-4% per ACC and ICCA projections.
- European asset rationalisation continues on structural energy-cost disadvantages, gradually rebalancing production towards emerging hubs such as India.
- Tightening sustainability regulation, including Europe's CBAM, penalises high-carbon imports — green manufacturing protocols (ZLD, renewable power integration) are becoming a condition of access to premium European and North American markets.
- India's real GDP grew 7.7% in FY 2025-26 on provisional estimates with FY 2026-27 projected at 6.8-7.2%, supported by domestic demand and public capital expenditure; the global economy is projected at 3.1% in CY 2026 and 3.2% in CY 2027.
- A USD 150 million multi-year supply agreement providing long-term earnings visibility over 4 years, with stable margins and high asset utilisation (elsewhere described as extending through March 2030 with a global agrochemical innovator, requiring no incremental capex).
- A residual 15-year long-term contract structure with a global customer, underpinned by a ₹200-250 Crs backward-integration project intended to deepen the relationship and drive margin growth over the long term.
- A strong pipeline of product qualifications and commercial discussions underway with customers across Europe and the U.S. following the India-EU FTA and improving U.S.-India trade dynamics.
- Increasing customer traction with a visible growth pipeline in the EV-linked PPS segment supporting the DCB capacity increase.
- Long-term methanol and toluene feedstock contracts across the GCC and Southeast Asia, plus a DCM Shriram chlorine supply partnership, securing input availability for the order pipeline (supply-side commitments rather than a customer order book).
- No conventional order book is disclosed — AIL reports contracted supply agreements and long-term customer contracts rather than an order-book value.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Despite 60%+ raw material inflation and Middle East export disruptions, Aarti delivered strong EBITDA (29% YoY) and PAT (43% YoY) growth via volume redirection, operational efficiencies, and new long-term contracts; the $150M agrochemical contract and INR200-250cr backward integration deal lock in earnings visibility, while Zone IV commissioning delays and FX revaluation losses are near-term headwinds.

open.item: FY26 tax rate expected to be a bit lower than mid-single digit.
Augene (Superform) JV expected to commission in June/July FY27 and ramp to full utilisation within the current financial year, contributing meaningfully.
China anti-involution benefit to PNCB/NCB chain products expected to start showing from Q1 FY27 onwards.
West Asia war curtailed Middle East shipments (~9-10% of revenue, mostly energy/MMA); full impact expected in the ongoing Q1 FY27, with volumes being rerouted to other geographies.
Recycling JV commissioning on track for CY26; technology proof to be established within the current financial year but not expected to contribute meaningfully to numbers yet.
Key raw materials (benzene, sulfur, aniline, toluene, methanol) up over 60%; expects to fully pass on price rise over 3-6 months provided RM stabilises; working capital normalisation to take time.
Gross block expected at ~Rs. 9,500-10,000 crore by end of FY27 when Zone-IV is fully commissioned.
Tax rate expected around 9-15% going forward (FY27), less volatile after prior-year tax litigation adjustments.
The previously-terminated dedicated contract asset (Dicamba intermediate, ~50% utilised) expected to see better utilisation in FY27 as US Dicamba volumes and lower tariffs support demand.
FY27 capex expected in the range of Rs. 700-800 crore, with significant part going to Zone-IV completion and the new backward-integration contract.

Zone-IV MPP and PEDA plants under commissioning trials to come on stream soon; entire Zone-IV (incl. five chemistry blocks) to commission phased through FY27, delayed 3-4 months due to labour constraints.
Contract-3 (10-year Specialty Chemical Intermediate) expected to ramp up to peak levels by FY27.
Rs. 300-450 crore capex-led EBITDA contribution maintained but may be delayed by ~6-7 months (beyond FY28) due to Zone-IV commissioning delay; cost initiatives EBITDA potential unchanged.
Net debt ~Rs. 4,300 crore (3.6x net debt/EBITDA); given lower capex intensity and improving cash flow, management targets net debt to decline in FY27, aiming towards 2.5x over 2 years.
DCB capacity debottlenecking continues to capture EV/PPS-driven demand; NCB debottlenecking under active consideration (not yet approved).
Company targets net working capital of 55-60 days on average (currently elevated due to RM prices and export mix).
MMA expansion to 360 KTPA on track and expected to be commissioned soon in line with market requirements.
Deploying AI and digital transformation tools across manufacturing plants targeting measurable gains in plant uptime and reduction in energy consumption.
CDMO effort underway with 3-4 projects at R&D level with global innovators; converting to concrete large-scale business seen as an 18-24 month journey.
Zone-IV/MPP new products targeted to be margin-accretive, aiming to restore 20%+ EBITDA margin profile of ~5 years back.
